headline: Washington Street project's $4.5 million cost and funding options presented; bond anticipation note to be explored.
summary: The city does not have that money today, so the presenter asked whether to bid the project on December 10th or wait. Work would start around the 15th or the end of March, and a presenter estimated the first payment at about $400,000 around April 15th. The city will look into a bond anticipation note and bring a recommendation back to council. The committee also approved buying a Life Pack 35 defibrillator for the fire department.
decisions: Approved buying one Life Pack 35 defibrillator for the fire department for $62,115.11.
discussion: Washington Street funding: Members asked whether the FY24 audit, not yet final, and the FY25 audit must be complete before a bond can be issued. Other questions covered cash flow for other high-need capital projects.

Project updates for residents: Members asked for regular impact updates, and a construction page for this phase would be added to the website. A presenter said flagging costs about $425 an hour, so the traffic plan uses one-way streets.
Sewer user fee credits: About $478,000 in credits went out first, with $475,815 more pending as sewer bills go out. Members asked whether recent bills were checked for accuracy.
Budget report format: Members discussed how often to review the monthly budget reports, such as quarterly finance committee meetings or a council presentation.

Budget report payroll delays: October payroll entries were not posted, and Maine paid family leave was set up wrong in the payroll system. The finance director said both would be fixed before the next monthly report.

decision_evidence.quote: motion to approve the purchase second then moved and seconded to approve the purchase all in favor thank you
